reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a dominant slow linear trend over longer windows, but local behavior is highly heterogeneous. At the shortest scale (2 points, 1 cycle), a clean monotonic rise is observed with no curvature. Over 6-point windows (3 cycles), two candidates show piecewise-linear shapes: one with a gentle rise followed by a plateau and slight dip (candidate 1), another with a steep drop to near-zero then flatline (candidate 2). The 10-point window (5 cycles, candidate 3) shows a sharp triangular peak centered at point 2853, rising from near-zero to ~19.5 and falling back within 3 points, followed by low-amplitude flat noise. All candidates share low roughness (<0.5) and near-zero baseline after the transient, suggesting stable post-event behavior. Amplitude varies widely (0.8–36), but the *shape* of transients—rapid ascent, brief apex, rapid descent—is consistent across candidates 2 and 3. Noise is minimal; no high-frequency jitter is present. Acceptable variation includes: (a) transient amplitude scaling, (b) exact timing of apex relative to window start, (c) post-peak decay slope. The consensus normal pattern is a brief, symmetric or slightly right-skewed impulse (duration ≤3 points) embedded in otherwise flat or slowly varying background, with no sustained oscillations or irregular jaggedness.

reference_profiles.description: Two-point strictly linear increase from 0 to ~26; no curvature, no noise, no context—pure slope. Represents minimal viable morphology for 1-cycle analysis.

Six-point piecewise linear: shallow descent → flat → gentle rise → peak at 956 → shallow decline. Moderate curvature (0.36), low amplitude (~0.9), stable baseline. Most representative of typical low-energy behavior.

Six-point steep drop from 35 to 0 in 1 step, then flatline. Extreme amplitude (27.4), high curvature (0.99), but morphologically simple: single impulsive decay. May reflect a high-magnitude normal event rather than anomaly.

Ten-point sharp symmetric triangle peak at center (2853), rising/falling in 2 points each, amplitude ~19.5, then flat low-noise tail. Highest curvature (1.01), moderate roughness. Best exemplar of canonical transient shape.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: For queries with short duration (<4 pts): match against candidate 0 (slope) or candidate 1 (piecewise). For queries showing a single sharp peak: prefer candidate 3’s triangular morphology; if amplitude is extreme but shape matches, still consider normal. Candidate 2 should only be used when query shows an abrupt drop-to-zero without recovery—treat as lower-confidence normal. Avoid using candidate 2 to normalize amplitude; use candidate 1 or 3 for scale reference.
uncertainties: Whether extreme-amplitude impulses (candidate 2) are truly normal or rare anomalies—requires cross-channel validation
Exact periodicity is ambiguous: catalog suggests period=2, but no clear repeating cycle appears in any candidate; transients may be aperiodic
Baseline drift vs. true trend: global trend exists per metadata, but local windows appear stationary after transients
